JOHN DENVER 1977 AUSTRALIA TOUR JACKET
$800

John Denver 1977 Australian Tour Crew Jacket — Attributed to RCA Recording Engineer Mickey Crofford.

Extremely rare original crew jacket from John Denver's 1977 Australian tour, featuring the embroidered “Celebrate John Denver Australia '77” tour emblem on the back and an original “Mickey” name patch on the front. The jacket was purchased several years ago from an eBay seller who represented it as having belonged to Mickey Crofford, John Denver's recording engineer during the 1970s. Friends of John Denver have personally confirmed that with me after I purchased it.

Made in the USA by Powderhorn Mountaineering in Jackson Hole, WY, this 65% polyester/35% cotton/nylon with 3M Scotchlite coating jacket is a men’s size M in excellent vintage like-new condition and valued between $1,000 - $1,500 with Heritage Auctions and RR Auction.

The back of the jacket is an embroidered patch with the 1977 tour logo. Front has a large front kangaroo/pouch pocket with a zippered compartment. The bottom of the jacket is a drawstring closure. It has been stored in a smoke-free/pet-free home for several years.

Mickey Crofford's association with John Denver is independently well established through contemporary recording credits and industry publications. Crofford's Denver recording credits are extensive. Among the recordings credited to him are “Back Home Again,” “Annie's Song,” “Thank God I'm a Country Boy,” “Sweet Surrender” and others. And critically, Crofford engineered Denver's 1977 album I Want to Live—the album from the very same year.

The price of this jacket is $800 with local pickup in the Grand Junction area, and I offer free delivery to any buyer attending the Aspen in October celebration this weekend between October 2 through October 4. I accept cash and Venmo.
